# z32 memo 1: obstruction-theoretic disproof routes are closed (O262)

Labels as in DISCOVERIES.md. ES is not solved; nothing here disproves or proves any case.

**Idea.** A counterexample n could in principle come from a local, Brauer–Manin (BM) or descent obstruction to
U_n(ℕ) ≠ ∅, where U_n : 4u₁u₂u₃ = n(u₁u₂ + u₁u₃ + u₂u₃).

**Literature (quoted from `sources/bright-loughran-1908.02526.pdf`).**
* Thm 1.6: Br U_n / Br ℚ ≅ ℤ/2, generated by the transcendental algebra (−u₁/u₃, −u₂/u₃).
* Thm 1.8 (1.4): (U_n(ℝ)₊ × ∏_p U_n(ℤ_p))^{Br} ≠ ∅ for every n — **no BM obstruction to ES at any n** (Thm 1.1).
  (1.5): the Br-set is a proper subset (a BM obstruction to strong approximation; Thms 1.2, 1.5 record it).
* Thm 1.9: U_n(ℚ) is not dense in U_n(𝔸)^{Br}_• — strong approximation fails beyond BM for every n (via
  non-Zariski-density of U_n(ℤ), real argument).
* Rem 1.10: the m/n surfaces are ℚ-isomorphic to U₁; analogues of Thms 1.5, 1.8, 1.9 hold.

**Consequence (PROVED, immediate from Thm 1.8).** Any ES counterexample is an integral Hasse failure *not*
explained by BM. Non-BM failures on the same ℚ-surface do exist for other numerators: 8/n fails at
n = 11, 17, 131, 241; 15/n at 32 values up to 20 521 (Pomerance–Weingartner Table 1, `sources/pw.txt`).
They are all small-n, small-count accidents.

**Exotic obstructions elsewhere (web search 2026-10-18).** Markoff surfaces: BM explains some integral Hasse
failures (Colliot-Thélène–Wei–Xu; Loughran–Mitankin, IMRN 2021), infinitely many are not explained by BM, and
Ghosh–Sarnak model them as a count of Γ-orbits being small; Dao (arXiv:2202.07142) gives more non-(algebraic-)BM
failures; Lyczak (AIF 2023) order-5 BM obstructions. No obstruction "beyond BM" for integral points is known that
is not at bottom a small count.

**Barrier screen.** B1/B5: BM is the T1 bit (Cor 1.4 = ET Prop 1.6). B6: n/a.

**Viability (Assessment).** As a disproof route: CLOSED — the only obstruction class is proved empty for ES, and
the non-BM failures are what the lottery (memos 4–5) prices. Promise 0/5.
